one_liner: Incremental streaming partial-JSON parser for LLM tool calls (Zig to WASM plus TypeScript); beats AI SDKs' re-parse-every-chunk loops.
what_it_does: An npm package (ESM, WASM embedded in the bundle) for JSON that arrives token by token: createParser() takes feed(chunk) and getValue() returns the growing partial object, createEventParser() fires callbacks on paths (on, onDelta for string deltas, onText for prose and think blocks around the JSON), and schema-driven picking skips fields a Zod-like schema does not name. It also offers a one-shot parse() that returns a lazy Proxy over a WASM tape, parsePartialJson, deepCompare and JSONL/JSON5 modes. It is not a JSON.parse replacement; it replaces the partial-JSON call inside an SDK's stream accumulation loop.
how_it_is_fast: It turns the O(n^2) pattern buffer += chunk; parsePartialJson(buffer) into O(n): each feed() appends bytes to a WASM buffer where a Zig structure tracker (bracket depth, string and escape state, 16-byte SIMD128 skip inside strings) updates completion status, and a JavaScript byte scanner (spScan) extends one mutable live object in place, so getValue() just returns the reference. The simdjson-derived zimdjson DOM parser compiled to WASM SIMD128 backs one-shot parse() and tape/Proxy access, not the streaming numbers.
when_to_use: Agent UIs that render partial tool_use or structured-output JSON on every token, payloads from about 1 KB up, where the SDK's partial parser re-parses the whole buffer (README on Bun: 11-14x at 1 KB, 31-47x at 5 KB, 660-2000x at 50-100 KB).
Field-level reactions while streaming: act as soon as the tool name completes, append a code string's new characters to an editor, abort the LLM stream early on a wrong tool.
Mixed LLM output with <think> blocks, code fences or prose around the JSON, which createEventParser skips to find the JSON value.
Reading a few fields from a multi-megabyte JSON document through the lazy Proxy (README: 2.3 vs 4.6 ms for one field of a 2.2 MB payload against JSON.parse).
when_not_to_use: One-shot parsing of complete JSON: JSON.parse is far faster on small inputs (1 KB: 2.16M vs 1.37K ops/s) and still slightly faster at 500 KB and 2 MB.
When streamed JSON must be validated: createParser only reports closing-bracket underflow as an error, and malformed scalar tokens become null.
When each chunk's partial must be an immutable snapshot (React state updates, diffing previous against current partial): getValue() hands back the same object, mutated by later feed() calls.
CommonJS-only projects or runtimes without WebAssembly SIMD128 (package is ESM-only, Node >= 20).
If an O(n) incremental JavaScript parser already fits (for example @streamparser/json, which the benchmark installs but never measures): the headline gap is algorithmic, not WASM or SIMD.

integration.form: npm module (ESM only; WASM embedded as base64, about 148 KB JS, 47 KB gzipped)
integration.dependencies: none at runtime; building from source needs Zig 0.15.2, Bun and wasm-opt
integration.min_toolchain: Node.js 20+, Bun, Deno, browsers or Cloudflare Workers with WebAssembly SIMD128
integration.platforms: any JavaScript runtime with WebAssembly SIMD128
integration.thread_safety: not documented; parser objects are single-threaded, and getTapeBuffer()/importTape() move parsed tapes between workers
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: replaces the partial-JSON call in an SDK accumulation loop (the benchmark ships patches for Vercel AI SDK, Anthropic SDK MessageStream and TanStack AI), but its API differs from JSON.parse and from each SDK's parser, and getValue() returns a live mutable object rather than a fresh snapshot

gotchas: Live object: while incomplete, getValue() returns the same object that later feed() calls mutate; clone it before storing a snapshot. That is also why the benchmark's 'both sides materialize a partial object per chunk' framing is uneven: stock parsers build a fresh object graph per chunk, VectorJSON returns a reference in O(1).

Weak validation in streaming mode: src/zig/stream.zig only flags '}'/']' underflow (it counts '{' and '[' together, so mismatched bracket kinds pass), and spScan in src/js/index.ts turns any scalar JSON.parse cannot read into null inside a try/catch, so malformed model output can finish as 'complete' with nulls instead of 'error'.

Docs contradict the code: the README 'How It Works' section and the benchmark's comment say each feed()/getValue() re-runs the SIMD parse over the accumulated buffer, but the code scans each new byte once (Zig structure tracker plus a JavaScript scanner) and zimdjson is only used for one-shot parse() and tapes, so WASM SIMD contributes little to the 14x-2028x figures.

Harness asymmetries: when a stock run is slow (warmup x 4 > 30 s, the 100 KB rows) the stock time is one cold warmup run while VectorJSON is the median of 3 after 2 warmups; Bun is 'latest' (unpinned) on an unnamed GitHub Actions CPU; the README one-shot rows give VectorJSON exactly 1.37K ops/s at both 1 KB and 10 KB, which points to a fixed per-call cost of about 0.7 ms in parse().
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over json-as (AssemblyScript JSON that beats JSON.parse on whole-document deserialization in V8) when input arrives as a token stream and you need partial objects or per-field events; for complete documents json-as or plain JSON.parse is faster.
verified_claims_summary: The project's CI benchmark (GitHub Actions ubuntu x86-64 runner, Bun latest, CPU unnamed) streams a synthetic JSON payload in 12-character chunks and reads a partial object after every chunk: stock parsers from Vercel AI SDK, Anthropic SDK 0.74.0, TanStack AI and partial-json re-parse the concatenated buffer each time, taking 3.2-3.9 ms at 1 KB and 6.1-13.4 s at 100 KB, against 283 us and 6.6 ms for VectorJSON's feed() plus getValue() (11x-2028x). Its one-shot parse() is slower than JSON.parse at every size measured.
status_note: Apache-2.0 npm package (0.5.1; 15 releases from 2026-02-16 to 2026-03-10), 18 stars, no issues filed and no commits since 2026-03-10, so 'active' is generous; easy to adopt for streaming UI work, but young, single-maintainer, and its streaming parser does not validate JSON grammar.
